name: Hydro
lede: Hydro is a muted grey-green from the 1930 Maerz and Paul dictionary, first recorded in 1920, and none of the color books we hold explains the name.

sections.title: A name with no recorded story
sections.body: Maerz and Paul's *Dictionary of Color* lists Hydro on plate 37 and records its first use in 1920, in the fashion and textile trade [1]. The swatch is a quiet green with a hint of blue, close to [[sea-green]] in feeling and far duller than [[viridian]] [1]. The origin of the name is undocumented. It may suggest water, but no source says so, so we leave it as a guess nobody can check.

sections.title: What the search turns up
sections.body:
Searching 29 color books for the word finds only the prefix *hydro-* in chemistry [2][3]. The Pigment Compendium uses it for hydrated and hydrocarbon materials, among them hydrocerussite, a lead carbonate [2]. Balfour-Paul's *Indigo* uses it in two places: chemists in 1898 showed that the plant's indican is hydrolysed to indoxyl, and a stable sodium hydrosulphite (dithionite) vat reducer arrived by 1904 [3].

These facts concern pigments and dyes, not the color Hydro, and no source connects them to the name [2][3]. We report them only to show the search was done and found nothing more.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch has a lightness of about 55 and a very low chroma of about 13, which is why it reads as a grey-green [1]. Its nearest archive color is Viridian, 10.0 units away, too far to count as a match [1]. We found no archive count for this swatch.
